one_month_reasoning: Window to 2026-11-05 contains Alphabet's Q3 print on Wednesday Oct 28 after the close (confirmed by the company 2026-10-06), so there are six trading days of post-earnings reaction inside the window. Microsoft, Meta and Amazon also report in late October and will re-price the AI-capex debate. Consensus is $3.03 EPS (Yahoo) on ~$127B revenue (TradingKey). Industry read-through into the print leans positive for Cloud: Wells Fargo models core Cloud +81% plus $9.2B of external TPU sales, and Constellation/Marvell news confirms the infrastructure cycle is intact. The main downside is the 2027 capex framework: the standing capex view puts Alphabet 2027 around $350B against a $285-357B consensus range, and a guide above it would be read as FCF-negative for longer. Search is two-sided (last tracker: clicks +13%, CPC +1%). Net: near-symmetric with fat tails, median ~$349 (+0.4%, small drift), a mixture of 85% at sigma 8.5% and 15% at sigma 17% for the earnings gap (unconditional ~9.9%, vs 32%/3.5 = 9.1% normal monthly vol). P(>= spot) 0.52.

fair_value.method: Blend at the Oct-2027 horizon: forward P/E at the 11-peer median (21.8x) on FY2028E core EPS of $17.5 (consensus $17.89 less ~$0.4 for capex-file base-case D&A) plus ~$17.8/share of net financial assets = $399 (weight 0.6), and a 2028E sum-of-the-parts (Services 18x after-tax OI, Cloud 7x 2028E sales, less capitalised Alphabet-level and Other Bets costs, plus net financial assets) = $326 (weight 0.4); blend ~$370.

EV/EBITDA is derived as MarketScreener EV/Sales x next-FY sales / next-FY EBITDA. Mega-cap subset (MSFT, AMZN, META, ORCL, AAPL) median 23.9x P/E, 10.8x EV/EBITDA. TTD was screened out: consensus revenue falls in 2026-27 and EPS is $0.34, so it is not a comparable growth or margin profile.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: GOOGL trades at 23.2x FY2027 headline, ~22.1x core after ~$17.8/share of financial assets, and 13.9x FY2027 EV/EBITDA (derived the same way), i.e. at the P/E median and above the EV/EBITDA median (GOOGL's EV/EBITDA is lifted because its EV of ~$4.15T is not reduced by most of the SpaceX and private stakes). I apply exactly the peer median, 21.8x, to FY2028 core EPS at the horizon.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: None applied. Arguments for a premium (Cloud +82% with a $513.9B backlog, external TPU sales, #1 Arena model) are offset by arguments for a discount (Q2 free cash flow negative, capex $195-205B in 2026 and 'significantly' higher in 2027, Search CPC +1% with incremental ad share going to Meta and Amazon, DC Circuit appeal). GOOGL's FY2028 consensus EPS growth (+19.7%) equals the mega-cap peer median, and its 2027 EBITDA margin (48.6% = $298.7B / $615.0B) is below META (58.9%) and MSFT (61.2%), so neither a persistent premium nor discount is evidenced.

thesis_break_reason: $245 is ~15.2x FY2027 consensus core EPS ($14.95) after ~$17.8/share of financial assets, below every mega-cap peer (lowest ORCL 21.4x) and between Baidu (13.2x, flat revenue) and Netflix (17.8x). The market would be pricing Search as ex-growth, and $245 is ~4% above the 52-week low of $235.84. Industry signals that would accompany a fundamental break: Broadcom or Marvell cutting custom-ASIC/TPU outlooks or hyperscalers signalling digestion (an AI-demand air pocket that would also stall Cloud backlog conversion), search-ad trackers showing Google spend growth below ~5% with CPC falling, or an adverse DC Circuit ruling on default payments. Capex anxiety alone has not taken the stock there.

reasoning: Delta refresh from 2026-10-02. No new filings. The Q3 print is now fixed for Oct 28, inside the 1-month window. The stock rose 1.2%, matching QQQ and the mega-cap peers, so price action since 10-02 carries no GOOGL-specific information. Industry read-through stays constructive for Cloud and TPU: the Constellation 20-year 890 MW uprate PPA plus 2,700 MW supply deal shows Alphabet contracting power years ahead (supplier-side confirmation of a long build-out, and a Gemini Enterprise customer win); Marvell's investor day lifted ASIC peers on the custom-silicon share thesis; Wells Fargo now sees $9.2B and $11.5B of external TPU sales in Q3/Q4. Gemini 4 Argon tops the Arena leaderboard and Polymarket moved Google to 42.5% for best model at end-2026. The ad side is unchanged: the last tracker (Tinuiti Q2) shows click-led Search growth with CPC +1%, and Meta and Amazon ads outgrew Search. Valuation: consensus FY27 rose to $14.95 and FY28 is verified at $17.89. I take $17.5 after a D&A adjustment for the standing capex view (Alphabet 2027 capex ~10% above consensus). The new 11-peer set gives a 21.8x median next-FY P/E; GOOGL's ~22.1x core multiple is already at the median and its FY28 growth matches the mega-cap median, so I apply 21.8x with no premium: P/E leg $399. I corrected my SOTP to deduct unallocated costs and moved it to the 2028 horizon: $326. Blend 60/40 = $370 (+6.4%). Distribution: two-piece lognormal, median ~$366, sigma ~0.30 up / 0.34 down (realised vol 32%), with fatter tails for regulatory and capex outcomes. The scenario mean ($375) is close to the ladder mean (~$379). Thesis break $245 (~15x core FY27, Baidu-to-Netflix territory). Research limits: Alpha Vantage was rate-limited, Twelve Data estimates are paywalled, DCD and Benzinga returned 403, and the Tinuiti Q3 report is not yet out. I did not use Anthropic stake-size claims (not disclosed in Alphabet filings) in any number.
